title: Lark Quarry dinosaur trackways, Winton Formation, Queensland
summary: At Lark Quarry, 95 km south-west of Winton in central-western Queensland, thousands of footprints in the mid-Cretaceous Winton Formation record dozens of dinosaurs on a river floodplain. Small ornithopod (Wintonopus) and small theropod (Skartopus) tracks are joined by large tracks once read as a theropod’s and reassessed in 2011 as an ornithopod’s. Sauropods such as Diamantinasaurus are known from the formation.

uncertainty.note: Romilio and Salisbury (2011) say late Albian–Cenomanian; Poropat et al. (2021) call the upper Winton Formation Cenomanian to possibly lowermost Turonian. Bounds here run from the Albian base to the Cenomanian top in the ICS chart. The id says 95 Ma; no opened page gives that figure.

as_recorded.value: Cenomanian to possibly lowermost Turonian (upper Winton Formation)

beats.caption: Rivers and a low-relief floodplain covered this part of Queensland while the Winton Formation formed, from late Albian to Cenomanian time.
Thulborn and Wade recognised three track types at Lark Quarry, named Wintonopus, Skartopus and cf. Tyrannosauropus.
A 2011 shape analysis argued the large tracks were made by an ornithopod, not a theropod, changing the trackmaker picture.
